events.title: Rider Advocate brief: 7 claims (0 void)
events.body:
C1: The driver cancelled the trip himself (cancelled_by = driver) at 09:15:05 and the $5.00 cancellation fee was charged to the rider, so the fee's legality is governed by NS-0 (driver-cancels, no-show branch) and NS-1. [F4 F7] [NS-0 NS-1]
C2: NS-1 (i) and (ii) are met: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:07:15 and at that moment he was 40 m from the pickup point, i.e. within the 200 m arrival radius, and the platform also recorded arrival at 09:06:20. [F5 F6] [NS-1]
C3: NS-1 (iii) is also met on the record, because after the "I'm Here" tap the driver stayed within 200 m of the pickup continuously for 7 min 50 s (well beyond 3:01) and until the 09:15:05 cancellation, with his car stationary 41 m from the pickup from 09:06:55 to 09:15:05 and no GPS gap. [F2 F3 F5 F6] [NS-1]
C4: The record's own no-show threshold was 8 minutes and it was reached: the driver messaged "8 min up, cancelling the trip" at 09:14 and cancelled at 09:15:05, 8 min 45 s after the platform-recorded arrival at 09:06:20, so the threshold criterion in NS-1's record-specific branch is satisfied as well. [F5 F10] [NS-1]
C5: The rider's own account shows a clean record (rating 4.7 over 3.2 years, zero no-show disputes upheld in 90 days), so there is no pattern of no-shows on the rider's side to support the fee. [F16] [NS-1]
C6: The driver's record shows 1 dispute upheld (no-show: 1) in the last 90 days, which supports flagging the account for review alongside the fee outcome, though it cannot by itself decide this case. [F17] [RD-6]
C7: No route-deviation or traffic excuse arises here (this is a no-show case; the driver never drove the trip), so RD-1/RD-2/RD-4 cannot be used to justify the fee, and the route profile is empty. [F13 F14] [RD-1 RD-4]
Weaknesses: NS-1 is drafted for the $6.61 rider cancellation fee, while the amount actually charged here is $5.00 (F7, F4); the policy has no clause establishing a $5.00 driver-cancellation no-show fee, so the driver will argue RD-6's flag_account (my C6) has no RD-2 refund > 0 to attach to and that the fee is simply an unpublished item to be waived under FARE-1 rather than refunded under NS-2. | The chat contains no rider message at all (F9, F10, F11) — the rider never messaged the driver, which the driver will use to argue the rider was unresponsive rather than 'coming out a minute later'; my complaint's 'a minute later' claim has no fact supporting it. | The threshold and wait conditions of NS-1 (iii) are in fact satisfied on the timeline (F5, F6), so the strongest honest defence is unavailable to me: on the face of the policy the $5.00/no-show position is against my client, and the only path to any relief is that $5.00 is an unpublished, non-conforming charge (F7) and/or that the case should go to a human because the fee amount does not match the NS-1 default.
Asks: refund_full $5.00

No route-deviation or traffic excuse arises here (this is a no-show case; the driver never drove the trip), so RD-1/RD-2/RD-4 cannot be used to justify the fee, and the route profile is empty.

weaknesses: NS-1 is drafted for the $6.61 rider cancellation fee, while the amount actually charged here is $5.00 (F7, F4); the policy has no clause establishing a $5.00 driver-cancellation no-show fee, so the driver will argue RD-6's flag_account (my C6) has no RD-2 refund > 0 to attach to and that the fee is simply an unpublished item to be waived under FARE-1 rather than refunded under NS-2.

The chat contains no rider message at all (F9, F10, F11) — the rider never messaged the driver, which the driver will use to argue the rider was unresponsive rather than 'coming out a minute later'; my complaint's 'a minute later' claim has no fact supporting it.

The threshold and wait conditions of NS-1 (iii) are in fact satisfied on the timeline (F5, F6), so the strongest honest defence is unavailable to me: on the face of the policy the $5.00/no-show position is against my client, and the only path to any relief is that $5.00 is an unpublished, non-conforming charge (F7) and/or that the case should go to a human because the fee amount does not match the NS-1 default.

claims.assertion: The rider did not show up: the driver's car sat stationary 41 m from the pickup point from 09:06:55 until the cancellation at 09:15:05, a continuous 8 min 10 s, and no trip was ever started.

Arrival was properly confirmed: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:07:15 while 40 m from the pickup point, well inside the 200 m arrival radius, so NS-1 (i) and (ii) are satisfied on the record itself; the platform's own arrival record agrees at 09:06:20.

The driver remained within 200 m of the pickup point for 7 min 50 s after the "I'm Here" tap and 8 min 45 s within 200 m before cancellation, so the continuous-wait requirement is met whether the threshold on the record is read as 8 minutes or the default 3 minutes.

The driver gave notice before cancelling: he announced "8 min up, cancelling the trip" at 09:14 and only cancelled at 09:15:05, past the 8-minute threshold on the record and far past the default 3-minute threshold.

The driver was contactable and not hiding: he messaged the rider at 09:07 identifying himself and his white Honda Vezel as being at the pickup point, so this is not the "stationary and uncontactable" abuse pattern NS-2 targets.
The amount charged is the published cancellation fee, recorded once at $5.00 with a 1.0x surge, so there is no duplicated or surge-inflated charge to unwind.
No record gap prevents verification of the wait: the chat record is complete with both messages timestamped and the timeline runs from recorded arrival through cancellation.

The driver's history is that of a high-volume, long-standing partner (1291 trips in 90 days, 6.5 years on platform) with one upheld no-show dispute and no route-deviation finding, which supports treating this as an ordinary no-show rather than button abuse; this is offered only as supporting context, not as the basis of the finding.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint states she came out only a minute after the cancellation (F4 shows cancellation at 09:15:05), so the other side will argue the driver cut the wait short; nothing in the record (F9, F10, F11) shows the rider ever replying to the driver's 09:07 or 09:14 messages, but equally nothing shows the driver tried any other reach-out before cancelling.

The driver's written statement that he 'waited the full 8 minutes the rule gives' (F12) is a statement, not a system record, so it cannot itself establish the threshold — the wait must stand on F2, F3 and F6, and on F10 only as to the 8-minute announcement.

The rider profile shows no upheld no-show disputes (F16), so she has no adverse history the driver can point to; by contrast the driver's own profile (F17) carries one upheld no-show dispute, which the other side may characterise as a pattern even though NS-2's flag_account branch is not triggered here because the tap was inside 200 m (F6).

points.response: Conceded as to the physical wait: the car was stationary 41 m from the pickup for 8 min 10 s (F3) and no trip started (F4). That satisfies the duration element, but NS-1 only ever authorises a $6.61 cancellation fee and the amount actually charged was $5.00 (F7), so the wait alone does not validate the charge.
Accepted: F6 shows the tap at 09:07:15 with the driver 40 m from the pickup, inside the 200 m radius, so NS-1 (i)-(ii) are made out and my C2 stands as stated.
Accepted on the wait: 7 min 50 s inside 200 m after the tap (F6) and 8 min 45 s cumulative (F2) exceed any threshold on the record, so NS-1 (iii) is met and I do not contest it.

The 09:14 message (F10) only proves the driver announced a cancellation; NS-1 makes the threshold turn on the recorded wait (F5, F6), not on the announcement. What the record does show is that the charge imposed was $5.00 (F7), an amount NS-0 and NS-1 never authorise.

This cuts against the driver rather than for him: a car standing 41 m from the pickup (F3) with the driver messaging "I'm here at the pickup point, white Honda Vezel" at 09:07 (F9) is a visible, contactable car, so nothing in the record explains the rider's delay; equally it does not defeat my client's point that the $5.00 charged (F7) has no basis in NS-0 or NS-1.

This is the crux and it helps my client, not the driver: NS-0 and NS-1 authorise a cancellation fee of $6.61 and nothing else, yet the fare record shows exactly $5.00 charged (F7) with no surge multiplier (F8). A $5.00 item appears in the policy only as the waiting-time fee under NS-6, whose conditions require the rider to have boarded and the trip to have completed, which is impossible here because the driver cancelled at 09:15:05 (F4).

Accepted: the chat is complete with both messages timestamped (F11) and the timeline covers arrival through cancellation (F5), so no evidence-gap argument is available to either side. That completeness is what lets the judge verify the $5.00 amount without witness accounts (F7).

Profile facts cannot decide the case, and this one is double-edged: F17 shows the driver already has one upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days, which is pattern evidence supporting a referral, while the rider's record is clean on no-shows (F16). Neither profile can establish that the $5.00 charge (F7) was valid.

I withdraw my suggestion that the money comes back under NS-2's refund_full branch: the tap was inside 200 m (F6), so button abuse is not shown. The rider's case rests on the amount instead: $5.00 was charged (F7) while NS-0 and NS-1 authorise only $6.61 in this scenario, and no NS-6 waiting fee can arise because the trip never completed (F4).

Agreed that the driver cancelled and the fee is governed by NS-0's driver-cancels/no-show branch, but the rider is wrong to say only NS-1's $6.61 rider-cancellation figure can ever be the consequence: NS-1's own conclusion is $6.61 only where the fee is a rider cancellation, and here the charged item is the $5.00 recorded at F7, so the branch must be applied to the item actually charged rather than to a figure the record does not contain.

Conceded: on F6 the "I'm Here" tap was made 40 m from the pickup point and F5 records platform arrival at 09:06:20, so NS-1 (i) and (ii) are satisfied — this point is not in dispute and confirms the driver was genuinely at the pickup point.

Conceded as to the wait: F6 shows 7 min 50 s within 200 m after the tap and F3 shows the car stationary 41 m from the pickup from 09:06:55 to 09:15:05 with no gap, so the continuous-wait requirement is met and the rider's own brief now concedes this.

Agreed and emphasised: F10 shows the driver announcing "8 min up, cancelling the trip" at 09:14 before cancelling at 09:15:05, so the threshold on the record was reached and the rider's "I came out a minute after" complaint (F4) is not supported by any fact — the rider never sent a single message (F11).

The rider's clean profile (F16) is accepted but proves nothing about this trip: profile facts cannot decide a case, and F16 also shows 0 upheld no-show disputes either way, so it neither supports nor defeats the fee.

I withdraw any reliance on the driver's profile and do not seek flag_account under RD-6: RD-6 requires RD-2 with a refund > 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach, and here there is no off-route segment and no refund (F13, F14), so F17 cannot support an account flag; the rider's own profile (F16) marks no abuse either.

Agreed: no traffic or route excuse is in play (F13, F14, F15), so RD-1/RD-2/RD-4 are irrelevant and the driver relies solely on NS-1 — which the rider's own brief concedes is satisfied on F2/F3/F5/F6.

The rider's only remaining path — that $5.00 is an unpublished item to be waived under FARE-1 — fails on the record in two ways: F7 shows a single recorded cancellation-fee line at the published figure with a neutral 1.0x multiplier (F8) and no additional or duplicated item, and the record itself labels the case a no-show with the threshold reached (F4, F5, F10); nothing in the fare facts shows a surcharge added beyond the fee, so there is nothing for FARE-1 to unwind.

Nothing wrong was found on your side, so no flag was placed on your account. The $5.00 comes back to you as a Ryde voucher.
